title: Minimum Time to Transport All Individuals
summary: Given n individuals who need to cross a river using a single boat that can carry at most k people at a time, and considering m environmental stages that affect the crossing time with speed multipliers mul[j], determine the minimum total time required for all individuals to cross the river.
statement: Given n individuals who need to cross a river using a single boat that can carry at most k people at a time, and considering m environmental stages that affect the crossing time with speed multipliers mul[j], determine the minimum total time required for all individuals to cross the river. Each stage j has a speed multiplier mul[j] that modifies the crossing time. The crossing time for a group g departing at stage j is the maximum of time[i] (the time it takes individual i to cross alone) multiplied by mul[j]. After a group crosses, the stage advances by floor(crossing_time) % m. If individuals are left behind, one person must return with the boat, taking time[r] × mul[current_stage] as the return time, and the stage advances by floor(return_time) % m. Return the minimum total time required for all individuals to cross, or -1 if it is not possible.
constraints: There are at most 12 people, boat capacity at most five, and at most five cyclic environment stages.
A crossing group moves at its slowest member time times the current multiplier; stages advance by the floored duration modulo m.
Unless everyone has crossed, one person on the destination side must return with the boat.
hints: A reusable state is the set of people across and the current environmental stage, with the boat back at base unless complete.
Run Dijkstra; each edge sends a capacity-bounded subset and, when needed, chooses any person across to return.
Precompute group slowest times, update stages with floor(duration) mod m, and relax combined crossing-return transitions.
Every legal strategy decomposes into these send-return cycles plus a final send, and all durations are nonnegative, so Dijkstra finds the minimum total time.
editorial: Every legal strategy decomposes into these send-return cycles plus a final send, and all durations are nonnegative, so Dijkstra finds the minimum total time.

tests.explanation: The lone person crosses at stage zero in five minutes.
The optimal send-return-send sequence takes 8 + 1.5 + 5 = 14.5 minutes.
